Acceleration

Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time and is a vector.

Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time. It is a vector, so a change in speed, direction, or both is acceleration. In calculus, acceleration is the derivative of velocity with respect to time. Because velocity is the derivative of position or displacement with respect to time, acceleration is the second derivative of position or displacement with respect to time. Common units include metres per second squared (m/s²) and feet per second squared (ft/s²).

The N.I.C.E. Design Process is a classroom design cycle used in these resources: Needs & Necessities → Investigate & Inquire → Create & Communicate → Evaluate → repeat. Velocity

Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time and is a vector.

Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time. It is a vector, so it has both magnitude and direction. The SI unit is metres per second (m/s); common everyday units can also include kilometres per hour (km/h) or miles per hour (mph) when a direction is included. For example, 100 km/h north while driving northbound on Highway 410 describes a velocity, while 100 km/h by itself describes only speed.
